summary.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.
Parallel-run fixed costs (~INR8.7 crore in Q1) expected to phase out as Gurgaon transition completes over coming quarters.
Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.
Standalone depreciation rose ~67% YoY, and management said standalone D&A increase was INR10-12 crore.
Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.
BESS (commercial and industrial, mostly under 0.5 MWh): ~15 MWh orders worth ~INR20 crore in hand and ~34 MWh (INR45 crore) in advanced pipeline.
EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated EBITDA swung from breakeven in Q4 FY26 to a INR22 crore loss in Q1; what drove the sequential drop and when does breakeven return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD20 million backlog as of 1 July plus new bookings and large strategic wins (double-digit million dollars, executing from calendar 2027 Q1) give confidence in 3x revenue growth and Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad was built for about 2x AC charger capacity and roughly 4,000 DC chargers. Utilisation is about 65% on DC chargers, close to 100% on AC chargers, 90-100% on DC power system lines, and close to 100% on PCBA and battery lines. AC charger monthly run rate is expected to rise about 50% over the next three months, and another AC line has been ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone depreciation rise, and what is the Tritium capitalisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. Its DRHP cited 60% wallbox share, and it estimates current wallbox share at north of 50%. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US Tritium factory capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US factory can service about USD100 million a year, about 2.5x the current ~USD10 million quarterly revenue, and it is running at about one-quarter of that today due to the ongoing turnaround.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven timing is not pinned down (Q2 or Q3 FY27), and Tritium breakeven is targeted only for Q4 FY27; the Tritium margin cushion from acquired low-cost inventory has already eroded.
Tritium strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX) are contingent on trial success and calendar 2026 conversion.

Working capital pressure from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations: elevated inventory and receivables, plus ~INR8.7 crore of Q1 parallel-run fixed costs expected to phase out over coming quarters.
Margin pressure from forex, commodity and US-led input cost increases on large orders, and supply disruption in semiconductors, plastics and copper.
Depreciation step-up (standalone +67% YoY, consolidated +57%) will weigh on PAT until plant utilisation and Tritium revenue scale.
Unresolved query on AC charger capacity figures (42,000 vs 222,000 units vs 2x expansion); management to revert with an exact answer.
Shift in EV growth from DC to AC chargers and reliance on Q4 pull-forward; watch whether standalone EV growth accelerates beyond 15% YoY.
key_quotes: So the overall performance on a stand-alone revenue rose by 57% year-on-year to INR237 crores and our EBITDA more than doubled to INR21 crores lifting the EBITDA margins to 8.8%.
But on a consolidated basis, the breakeven may be over the next 2 quarters itself. I can't specify whether quarter 2 or 3.
Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption.
So I think it's just a timing issue. But this growth is not 1x. It's continuing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, Tritium turnaround and the Hyderabad capacity build-out, but cautious on timing, as management repeatedly declined to specify exact quarters for breakeven. Some answers were loose or deflected (for example the capacity-figure reconciliation and blended EV market share), with the management promising to revert.
